ada: quick heads-up — nightly profiler shows OOM spikes on the canary after the kernel-selection change (nvf32 -> quant8-ish path). looks like prompt/prefix prefetch is duplicating KV entries while workspace fragmentation increases. p50 token latency fine, p95 up ~1.6x.
infra-bot: [ALERT] canary-182: OOM on gpusrv-12 (pod redwood-runtime-canary) 2026-03-18T03:21Z
sam: can you attach the allocator snapshot + the per-kernel workspace footprints? want to see free-list churn.
ada: pasted the snapshots below — allocator histogram + prefetch counters:
```
allocator.slabs: {64MB:12, 32MB:23, 8MB:118}
workspace.pool.reused: 27%
kv.prefetch.dup: 3.1% (measured over 20s window)
kernel.active: quant8_fast (fallback to nvf32 when OOM)
```
jonah: that ~3% KV duplication on its own seems small, but after the kernel change workspace footprint jumped ~24% so we see more slab splintering and new allocations per-request. batching heuristics also changed: dynamic-batch-size cap increased which forces larger temporary buffers.
maria: ran a quick TTL/shard sweep earlier: ttl=60s -> ttl=20s reduced steady mem by ~12% but hit rate dropped ~4.7 percentage points. shrinking shard count 128->64 lowered tail OOM frequency in the sims but increased miss rate for long-lived sessions.
kai: proposal — adaptive prefetch window that scales with active sequence length and allocator slack. pseudo-config:
```
prefetch.window = max(1, min(6, floor(3 * mean_active_seq_len / 512)))
// also throttle prefetch when allocator.free_ratio < 0.15
```
This keeps duplication <1% in sims and avoids aggressive KV duplication on kernel-induced footprint increases.
sam: +1. also try bumping the workspace pool temporarily during kernel switch instead of creating new slabs immediately. small config to try:
```
workspace.pool.target = 256MB
allocator.fragmentation_threshold = 0.20
on_kernel_switch: pool.grow_temp = true
```
ada: plan: run two canary experiments tonight — A) adaptive prefetch + transient workspace bump, B) conservative TTL (20s) + reduce shard count + kernel fallback policy. will capture allocator metrics, hit/miss, and latency tails.
maria: make sure the eval harness includes our regression prompts so we catch any quality drift when we fall back to nvf32. also capture per-token cost delta.
ada: ack — will post the canary results tomorrow morning. tagging @sam @maria @jonah for visibility. :thumbsup:
